key_insight: Ideal liquid crystal elastomer theory links molecular anisotropy to reversible actuation and soft deformation through a continuous family of stress-free states.
engineering_relevance: This framework supports constitutive modeling of LCE actuators and compliant structures whose mechanical response depends on mesogen alignment and stretch.
method: Connect anisotropic Gaussian-chain statistics to neo-classical continuum elasticity.
Use quasi-convex relaxation to describe domain coexistence and three stretch-dependent macroscopic phases.
Outline extensions for thermal and optical coupling, director distortion, network nonideality, and viscoelasticity.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a theoretical review and phase classification, without reporting datasets, quantitative benchmarks, or experimental validation.
watch_item: Ideal soft elasticity assumes no memory of the crosslinking state; realistic networks may require nonideal and rate-dependent constitutive terms.
paper_title: Elastic theory of ideal liquid crystal elastomers
